label: How the noise level gets in: shift, scale, gate
context: Show one layer's feature vector as a row of 16 vertical bars (activations) in the middle of the canvas. On the left a small σ dial, rotating through low and high values. From the dial an arrow goes to a box 'MLP(σ)' that outputs three small coloured vectors labelled γ (scale), β (shift), α (gate). Phases: (1) 'normalise': bars are standardised to zero mean, unit spread; (2) 'scale and shift: (1 + γ)·h + β': bars stretch and move, differently for low and high σ as the dial turns; (3) 'gate: x + α·F(h)': a residual stream bar row above receives the update multiplied by α; show α starting at 0 ('adaLN-Zero: the block starts as the identity, nothing changes') and growing during 'training' (a small progress bar labelled training) until the update is visible. Colour the conditioning path warm #B4552F, features blue #0B4FC0. Canvas is responsive: width anywhere from 340 to 900 px, height 400 px; derive every size and position from width and height, keep all text at least 11 px and fully inside the canvas, and on narrow widths stack or shrink rather than overlap. Loop forever on a cycle of 10 to 16 s with smooth easing between phases. White background. Put a one-line phase caption at the top centre that changes with the phase. No title inside the canvas (the card has one). Use plain sans-serif labels.

spec.title: How the noise level gets in: shift, scale, gate
spec.caption: A noise level σ goes through MLP(σ) to give γ (scale), β (shift) and α (gate). The features are normalised, then scaled and shifted as (1 + γ)·h + β, and the block update is added to the residual stream as x + α·F(h). With adaLN-Zero, α starts at 0, so the block is the identity. Training grows α until the update shows.
